prerequisites: It is advisable to have acquired basic knowledge of biology and cell structure.

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the morphological organization of the human body at various levels (cells, tissues, organs, systems).
Know the main determinants of health and environmental and occupational risks.
Analyse the main prevention and safety strategies in the workplace.
Collaborate with healthcare figures in the design and evaluation of biomedical technological solutions.

syllabus_topics: Definition and content of hygiene and public health
Health and disease indicators, risk factors
Prevention strategies (reporting, isolation, disinfection, sterilisation, prophylaxis, disinfestation)
Classification of risks in the workplace
Prevention and protection strategies for risk reduction
Structure and function of the human cell
Morphological and functional characteristics of the main tissues: epithelial, connective, muscular and nervous
Organisation of the human body: terminology and anatomical planes
Morphological and functional characteristics of the skeletal and joint systems
General information on the structure of the vascular system: arteries, veins and capillaries
Morphological and functional references of the main systems: cardiovascular, respiratory, digestive, urinary, genital, endocrine and nervous
teaching_methods: Possible use of interactive tools and digital anatomical tables (Anatomage)
assessment_rules: The mandatory oral examination verifies the ability to analyse risk factors and preventive measures, and the understanding of the morphological and functional organization of the human body. The final grade will be calculated as the weighted average of the results obtained in the two modules.
